title: Understanding L0 Regularization
text: L0 regularization limits the number of non-zero parameters in the model. Think about how this constraint affects the model's ability to fit the data. What happens when only one parameter can be non-zero?

title: Logistic Regression Basics
text: In logistic regression, the output is a probability that a given input point belongs to a particular class. The logistic function, or sigmoid function, is used to map predicted values to probabilities. Remember that the sigmoid function is defined as $$\frac{1}{1+e^{\left(-z\right)}}$$.

title: Rounding Probabilities
text: Once you have the predicted probabilities from the logistic regression model, you need to round them to the nearest whole number to make a classification decision. Consider how this rounding affects the classification of each data point.

title: Choosing the Non-Zero Parameter
text: If you can only have one non-zero parameter, which color should you choose to minimize misclassification?

title: Calculating Misclassifications
text: After choosing the non-zero parameter, calculate how many data points are misclassified. Remember to round the predicted probabilities to the nearest whole number.
